Who this class is for

For anyone who feels they’ve tried everything

  • People who have cut out food after food, and whose list of “safe” meals keeps getting shorter.
  • Anyone who tried low FODMAP from a printout and was never shown how to bring foods back.
  • People who have tried probiotics, apps and advice online, and want to know what the evidence says.
  • Anyone who wants a clear, step-by-step method from a dietitian, not another list of foods to avoid.

Here’s what you’ll learn

Five things we’ll cover together, live

Gut health foundations

What an IBS diagnosis does and doesn’t tell you, and why getting the right diagnosis comes before any diet change.

The low FODMAP diet in three stages

Restrict, reintroduce, personalise. Why it was designed to be temporary, and why so many people stop after stage one.

The most common IBS diet mistakes

The ones I see again and again in clinic, from cutting foods without a plan to skipping reintroduction.

Pivot or stay

What a dietitian looks at when low FODMAP doesn’t help, including SIBO and histamine intolerance, and when to speak to your doctor.

Eating normally again

Shopping, eating out and travel, and how to build a diet that is as varied as possible for the long term.

Questions

Before you save your seat

Who is this class for?

Adults who want to understand the low FODMAP diet and how dietitians approach IBS, step by step. It isn’t suitable as a substitute for one-to-one care if you are pregnant, under 16 or have an eating disorder.

What if I can’t make it live?

Register anyway. Everyone who signs up gets the replay.

Is this medical advice?

No. It’s an educational class. Please speak to your GP about any new or changing symptoms.

Why is it free?

Because the first step should be easy. Come, take what helps, and decide afterwards if you want more support.

Ad creatives · Video scripts · Meta

Video ad scripts

Three talking-to-camera scripts, each around 30 to 45 seconds, in your own voice. Each ends with an on-screen “Educational content, not medical advice.”

Script 1 · “Never meant to be forever”

Hook (0 to 3s)

“The low FODMAP diet was designed to be temporary. Here’s the part most people miss.”

Body

“Low FODMAP has three stages. Restrict, for a short time. Reintroduce, one group at a time. Then personalise, so the diet is as varied as possible. A lot of people only ever do stage one, from a list online, and stay there.”

CTA

“I’m running a free live masterclass where I walk through all three stages as a dietitian. Tap Sign up to save your seat. The replay is included.”

Shot: talking to camera, orange backdrop, on-screen text “Restrict · Reintroduce · Personalise”.

Script 2 · “Pivot or stay”

Hook (0 to 3s)

“Low FODMAP doesn’t help everyone. A dietitian explains why.”

Body

“When low FODMAP doesn’t make a difference, that’s useful information. In clinic, that’s when we pivot and look at other areas, like SIBO or histamine intolerance, always after a proper diagnosis from a doctor.”

CTA

“In my free class I explain how dietitians make that decision. Tap Sign up below.”

Shot: talking to camera, cut to a simple “Pivot or stay?” graphic in teal.

Script 3 · “The mistakes I see most”

Hook (0 to 3s)

“As an IBS dietitian, these are the mistakes I see most often.”

Body

“One: cutting out foods without a plan to bring them back. Two: skipping reintroduction altogether. Three: changing diet before getting the right diagnosis. Each one is easy to fix once you know the method.”

CTA

“Join my free live class, the Take Control Masterclass. Sixty minutes, replay included. Tap Sign up to save your seat.”

Shot: talking to camera, counting on fingers, numbers 1 to 3 on screen.
